answer: Seven reviewers drawn from the lotus roster file scores in velvet envelopes opened when all seven are in, and a verdict stands if the nadir gap, lowest to median, is at most one point; a wider gap triggers a panel and freezes stakes. Each fake reviewer posts its 40-credit stake, one stake per seat, and loses 20 credits for a deviating grade. Rented seats fail: sealed ballots hide compliance, the nadir rule forces corrupting all seven, and expelled seats need fresh replacements. The k-th fake costs 40 plus 2(k-1) credits, so 1,000 cost 1,039,000; an honest reviewer posts one 40-credit stake.
